newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bankers' chief supports financial reforms.
newsitem.headline: Japan bankers' chief supports financial reforms.

text.p: Shunsaku Hashimoto, chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan, said on Tuesday that he basically supports a financial system reform plan unveiled on Monday.
"Japan should set up global standards soon in order to activate Japanese financial markets," Hashimoto told reporters, adding that this was his personal opinion.
He said he agreed with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that early reform should be implemented, including that of market structure.

Bankers' federation chairman Hashimoto, who is also the president of Sakura Bank Ltd, said, however, it was regrettable that the reform plan did not include an overhaul of public-sector financial institutions, such as the postal savings system.
Prime Minister Hashimoto announced a five-year plan on Monday to liberalise Japan's financial markets.
The moves would allow banks, securities houses and insurance companies to enter each others now-protected sectors and end fixed commissions for stock brokers.
Hashimoto said Japan's government-run postal savings system was an obstacle to the reform of the private-sector financial system.
He said the administrative reform process should include considering privatisation of the postal savings system, he said.
